punchline: Airlines move huge crowds every day and keep a tiny profit per trip, while Google, with far less revenue, kept a big share of what it earned.
thirty_sec: Peter Thiel has a blunt line: competition is for losers. Look at airlines. They carry enormous numbers of people, create huge value, and keep only a tiny profit per passenger trip, because rivals keep competing it away. Google, in the same year, had far less revenue but kept a large share as profit. Why? Nobody came close to it in search. His advice: stop copying what works and build something new, starting in a small market you can own.
question: What's something you do that people couldn't easily get from anyone else?
